implementation: Winograd F(2x2,3x3) and F(4x4,3x3); CPU constant-weight pretransform, GPU input transform, existing batched GEMM, GPU inverse transform with bias/clamp
weightPacking: Once when loading the model, outside warmup and measurement. Original weights are unmodified.
scratch: Two shared graph buffers reused sequentially by every transformed convolution. No per-frame allocation.
precision: Transforms and GEMM operate in FP32; FP16 graphs round the output to FP16. This limits overflow and cancellation in the transforms.

accuracy.cpuOracle: 12 cases: FP32/FP16, both tile sizes, odd channel counts, multiple batches, non-square spatial tails, no padding/one-pixel padding/two-pixel padding, bias/no-bias, clamp/no-clamp and one-pixel outputs
accuracy.fullModel: Both tile sizes and precisions pass the existing committed PyTorch DepthART reference tolerances without relaxation.
accuracy.cameraPipeline: F4 FP16 preprocess -> full model -> depth stats -> draw passes circle/gradient/black/white frames against the FP32 reference. Grayscale tolerance remains one byte.
accuracy.chromeExample: Synthetic animated video input; both FP32 and FP16 Winograd pipelines reach camera live and produce frame metrics; precision switching succeeds.

decision: F4 is available via ?winograd=4 in the DepthART example. F2 remains a benchmark control because it provides little FP32 gain and regresses FP16 locally. Neither path changes production defaults pending more hardware measurements and evaluation of scratch memory cost.
remainingLimitation: The existing tiled GEMM is reused unchanged. Full transformed intermediates add memory traffic; measured full-model gains are well below the multiplication reduction and below 2x.
